intro: Five threads worth watching across drug development this week — a clear point of view, with the sources to back it. Refreshed every Monday.

narratives.headline: Protein degraders have moved from promise to frontline pharma capital
narratives.detail: Roche's $700M upfront (up to $2.3B) for Nurix's BTK-degrader is the second large-cap degrader transaction this window, and Roche optioned immunology and neurology on top of the oncology lead. That promotes protein degradation from emerging-modality watch to a confirmed, multi-TA platform with frontline-pharma capital behind it — no longer an early-stage bet.

narratives.headline: KRAS is now a three-class target
narratives.detail: J&J paid $1B in cash for preclinical Firefly Bio, pricing a KRAS-targeting ADC before a single patient is dosed and anchoring the deal on Bertozzi bioorthogonal chemistry. Covalent inhibitors, RAS(ON) agents and now ADCs are all chasing the target everyone spent a decade calling undruggable.

narratives.headline: The incretin tolerability ceiling is now Phase 3-anchored
narratives.detail: Survodutide's ~19% discontinuation rate in SYNCHRONIZE-1 runs roughly 2.5–5x the Phase 2 class baseline, and Boehringer's 'consistent with class' defence quietly extends that ceiling across the GLP-1/glucagon tier. With ENDO 2026 days out, it reads as a live constraint on retatrutide and CagriSema — not a footnote.

narratives.headline: Hepatology fibrosis-regression opens a new target axis
narratives.detail: GSK's UK liver-fibrosis pact with Engitix is the first hepatology-fibrosis macro signal in twelve cycles, and it's framed around mechanism of regression rather than the steatosis-and-inflammation playbook of NASH/MASH. It's early and discovery-stage, but it marks target diversification beyond cardiometabolic into fibrosis biology — worth tracking before it gets crowded.

narratives.headline: M&A heat is sustained at the top end — even in a 'quiet' month
narratives.detail: Seven multibillion-dollar takeouts closed in a May that trade press called quiet, and the cycles since have kept adding deals across oncology, hepatology and rare disease. By deal count it looks slow; weighted by value, the top end is plainly still active. Deal-value, not deal-count, is the indicator that's holding.
